title: Units modulo powers on an affine curve
statement:
Let $C$ be a smooth affine connected curve
over an algebraically closed field $k$, and let $n\geq1$.
Then $\mathcal O_C(C)^\times/\mathcal O_C(C)^\times{}^{\,n}$
is finite.

proof.text: Choose $C\subseteq\overline C$ with finite complement $S$ by [lem-sc-compactification]. Regard a unit on $C$ as a rational function on $\overline C$ (the open immersion is dense because $C$ is a nonempty connected curve). By the divisor exactness in [lem-sc-divisor-sequence-general], a rational function on $\overline C$ whose divisor is zero is a regular unit on $\overline C$; applying this to a unit and its inverse shows that the kernel of the divisor map on $\mathcal O_C(C)^\times$ is $H^0(\overline C,\mathcal O_{\overline C})^\times=k^\times$ by [lem-sc-global-functions]. The divisor of a unit has zero valuation at every point of $C$ (the unit and its inverse are regular there), so it is supported on $S$; the finite-support assertion is also recorded in [lem-sc-divisor-finite-support]. Thus the divisor map identifies $\mathcal O_C(C)^\times/k^\times$ with a subgroup $L$ of the finite-rank free group $\bigoplus_{P\in S}\mathbf Z[P]$. By [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free], $L$ is free of finite rank. Choosing a finite basis of $L$, every class in $L/nL$ is represented by one of the finitely many combinations with coefficients in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, so $L/nL$ is finite. The divisor map induces a surjection from $\mathcal O_C(C)^\times/\mathcal O_C(C)^\times{}^{\,n}$ onto $L/nL$. If $\operatorname{div}(u)=n\operatorname{div}(v)$ for units $u,v$, then $u/v^n$ lies in the kernel, hence in $k^\times$; an $n$-th root exists in $k$ because $k$ is algebraically closed, so $u$ is an $n$-th power. The induced map is therefore injective as well, and the desired quotient is finite.
